zotero.abstractNote: Offline reinforcement learning (RL) aims to learn optimal policies from static datasets. A major challenge in this setting is the presence of hidden confounders, which violate the standard assumption of unconfoundedness and lead to biased policy evaluation and sub-optimal policy learning. While recent works have addressed this by leveraging instrumental variables or proxy variables, they often rely on strong identifiability assumptions that are difficult to satisfy in practice. In this work, we introduce Delphic, a novel framework for offline RL under nonidentifiable hidden confounding. Delphic leverages the structure of the causal graph to learn a representation that is invariant to the hidden confounder, while still being predictive of the reward. We provide theoretical guarantees for the identifiability of the optimal policy under our framework and demonstrate its effectiveness on a range of challenging offline RL benchmarks.
